title: Logic and computation with Python
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn Python from scratch by building logic tools: values, conditionals, loops, functions, lists, tuples, strings, dictionaries, sets and recursion, used to represent formulas, evaluate them, print truth tables, test validity and equivalence, convert to normal forms, decide satisfiability by search, check simple proofs and evaluate first-order sentences in finite models.

weeks.1: Python basics: values, variables, expressions and printing
weeks.2: Booleans and conditionals: Python's logical operators
weeks.9: Normal forms: negation normal form, CNF and DNF
weeks.11: Sets and dictionaries: finite first-order models
weeks.12: Checking natural deduction proofs line by line

blocks.deliverable: Write five programs that use if, and, or and not.
Write functions for the conditional and the biconditional.
Write an evaluator for propositional formulas.
Week 7 midterm; print a complete truth table for any formula.
Convert formulas to CNF and check the result.
Evaluate quantified sentences in a finite model.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Logic toolkit: build and test a small Python module that represents propositional formulas, prints truth tables, decides tautology, entailment and equivalence, converts to CNF, finds countermodels and evaluates first-order sentences in finite models, with a test suite and a short user guide.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
